doc:
End-of-queue chain re-analysis (plan change C16b): the end of the queue as a chain of stuck-alone agents.

Input:  data/E1/E1_runs.jsonl (both modes, 200 seeds each), data/derived/E1_keystone.json (second-trap class).
Output: data/derived/E1_chain.json.

Definitions (as experiments/E1/e1_analyze.py)
  stuck-alone   margin_C1 = g_max(r) - m v0 / tau > 0; passable = margin_C1 <= 0.
  arrival       first entry into the door zone (field "arrive": t, n_active, behind_1m, order).
  active at t   spawned and not exited by t (exit_t[j] > t, or never exited).
  exited        the agent exits before the run stops (completion, deadlock or 600 s cap).
(a) per run: the arrival sequence (stuck-alone flags in arrival order); stuck-alone fraction by arrival decile
    (decile of the arrival rank within the run, over agents that arrived); the length of the final run of
    consecutive stuck-alone arrivals (deadlocked runs and all runs); the margin of the k-th last arrival;
    succession in the second-trap class: K1b target held alone, its margin and arrival order relative to the
    blocker.
(b) for each stuck-alone agent at its door-zone arrival, predictors of exit, each by ROC AUC (Mann-Whitney, ties
    1/2; positive class = exited) with a 95% CI from 2000 resamples of seeds (percentile, PCG64(12345)):
      others_active         n_active - 1 (the k = 3 rule's score);
      behind_1m             agents within 1 m behind (recorded at arrival);
      passable_active       other agents with margin <= 0 still active;
      stuck_active          other stuck-alone agents still active.
    Also: the best single-threshold accuracy of each count score (exit iff score >= k), the exit rate by
    (passable_active, stuck_active) cell, and the all-exit baseline.
(c) the physical reading tested, with its numbers (field "c_reading").

b_exit_rate_by_passable_x_stuck.note: keys 'p<passable_active>|s<stuck_active>', each capped at 3 (3 = 3 or more); value [exited, n]
keys 'p<passable_active>|s<stuck_active>', each capped at 3 (3 = 3 or more); value [exited, n]

c_reading: E1a: stuck-alone fraction rises from 0.19 in the first arrival decile to 0.64 in the last; the last five arrivals have median margin 43 N (rest -62 N). Exit AUC: passable_active 0.938 [0.931, 0.946], others_active 0.974, stuck_active 0.960, behind_1m 0.926. With no passable agent left, 210/371 stuck-alone arrivals exit; with at least one, 3969/4115. Second trap: K1b held in 145/154, target stuck alone in 145 of those.

E1b: stuck-alone fraction rises from 0.20 in the first arrival decile to 0.62 in the last; the last five arrivals have median margin 38 N (rest -62 N). Exit AUC: passable_active 0.948 [0.941, 0.955], others_active 0.975, stuck_active 0.963, behind_1m 0.925. With no passable agent left, 141/288 stuck-alone arrivals exit; with at least one, 4014/4177. Second trap: K1b held in 151/160, target stuck alone in 151 of those.

Verdict (E1b). Supported: passable agents drain first, so the last arrivals are enriched in stuck-alone agents (0.62 in the last arrival decile against 0.14-0.20 in the first eight; the final blocker is among the last three arrivals in 184/196 deadlocked runs). Not supported: that only passable agents can push a stuck-alone agent through. With no passable agent left, 141/288 stuck-alone arrivals still exit (131/178 when three or more stuck-alone agents are still in the room), and stuck-alone pushers predict exit at least as well (AUC 0.963 against 0.948 for passable ones). Cleanest statement: a stuck-alone agent is pushed through by whoever is still in the room, whether or not those agents could pass alone; the total count is the best single predictor (AUC 0.975, [0.970, 0.979]), and the chain ends when fewer than about three others are still in the room as the last stuck-alone agent arrives.
